correctness.rationale: On the 2n vertices, d((i,a),(j,b))=min(|i-j|,n-|i-j|)+|a-b| gives symmetric/antisymmetric cyclic Fourier blocks. For t>=1, elementary Gaussian geometric bounds prove all symmetric modes positive and order antisymmetric modes strictly with angle, giving a unique last eigenvalue F_n(t). Its derivative is >exp(-t)/2. Uniform n>=20 estimates establish F_n(1)<0, and F_n(t)->1, yielding a unique critical root, exact nullity parity and all-t last-failure supremum. Uniform Gaussian tails plus fourth-order theta expansion prove t_even=t_*+O(exp(-n^2/4)) and t_odd=t_*-pi^2 Q(t_*)/[F'(t_*)n^2]+O(n^-4). The embedded standalone checker was executed from the current new package source and compared direct kernel matrix multiplications with finite Fourier eigenvalues on ten orders; finite tests are auxiliary, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Gaussian kernels of squared intrinsic graph distance are not automatically positive semidefinite. For the canonical circular ladder C_n square K_2, this theorem identifies an exact final admissibility threshold for every n>=20, its nonzero infinite-length limit, and a concrete parity obstruction with n^-2 drift and endpoint nullity jump. Compared with known isolated-cycle vanishing and wheel growing thresholds, this is a new structural regime relevant to finite graph covariance construction and Fourier positive type, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
